selected.rationale: The Fitness Enthusiast focuses heavily on activewear, technical fabrics, and performance claims, which aligns directly with the advertiser's technical outerwear shells priced at $650+. They can be effectively reached on Cloudfoot (pub_017).

The Sustainability Buyer values supply chain transparency and specific sustainability claims, matching the advertiser's focus on craftsmanship and professional-grade durability. They match the audience profile of Stride & Stem (pub_016).

The Affluent Classic has low price sensitivity and high AOV ($145), aligning with the luxury tier and craftsmanship value of $650+ ski shells. They are a strong demographic match for publishers like Marlowe & Co. (pub_004) and Linden Park (pub_005).

rejected.reason: The Wellness Optimizer focuses on wellness, clean beauty, and supplements rather than technical outerwear, and their typical AOV of $95 is far too low for a $650 luxury item.
The Busy Parent looks for convenience, meal kits, and family-friendly items, and explicitly dislikes luxury positioning, making them a poor fit for a $650 technical ski shell.
The Gen Z Aesthete has a typical AOV of $48 and focuses on fast-moving trends and beauty, which does not match the heavy-duty performance and luxury price tier of backcountry ski patroller shells.
The Pet Parent is entirely focused on pet food, supplies, and health, sharing no category overlap with technical apparel.
The Convenience-First Millennial prioritizes instant delivery, subscriptions, and quick commerce, whereas the advertiser operates on a one-off, high-consideration luxury business model.
The Value-Conscious Shopper has high price sensitivity and responds to discount-forward messaging and bundles, directly conflicting with a $650+ luxury price point.
The Gifter is looking for gift sets and last-minute presentation items rather than specialized technical outdoor gear for serious backcountry skiing.
